text:
Jake Evans was a seventh-round pick who became the kind of center coaches like having. This month he has become a little more than that. His ice time over the last ten games is up 2.7 minutes to 17.3 a night, and he has 2 goals and 3 assists in that stretch, including a game-winner on Nov. 12 and the go-ahead goal against Winnipeg on Nov. 19.

For the season he has 4 goals and 5 assists in 23 games. Montreal controls 55% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on, the share of chance quality, 6 points better than when he sits.

Some of it is running hot. His shooting percentage is 20% against a range of about 12% to 17% for him, and the Canadiens have scored 3.5 more goals than their chances deserve with him out there. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level, so we would not expect this pace to hold in full. But the minutes are the real signal: a coaching staff giving a checking center more ice is telling you what it thinks.
headline: More minutes, more goals
